title: Codex, data analysis, and deep research

opening.headline: When you want to entrust data organization and receive a research report even if you don't know code, you will learn how to decide what to use among codex, data analysis, and in-depth research.
body: The column names in the Excel file are different, so merging and tallying is repeated over and over again. Market research requires opening dozens of sites and comparing them. You may be wondering if there is a feature that allows you to do this without having to write the code yourself.

ChatGPT has several features with similar-sounding names. In this class, we will look at data analysis that turns uploaded files into tables and charts, Codex, a coding agent in charge of software development, and in-depth research that compiles multiple sources to create a report with citations. Next, we explain an example of selecting an appropriate function based on the length of the work and the needs of the evidence.
objectives: Can explain the role of Codex, data analysis, and in-depth research
You can distinguish between functions that fit the nature of the job.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: I want to organize data and receive reports without having to know code.
screens.lead: Let's look at two work situations. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

items.answer: Because the column names are different in each file, it takes time to merge them, and after merging, aggregation and chart creation are repeated. It would be a great help if you could process it as a question rather than writing the formula yourself.

items.prompt: Situation 2: Receiving a market research report
items.answer: Researching competing services requires opening dozens of sites to compare prices and features. It can take a day just to read and organize the sources.

items.prompt: How do you choose when you have three features with similar names?
items.answer: Data analysis, in-depth research, and Codex all sound like 'functions that leave work to AI,' but they are different tasks. The criteria are whether you handle files, compile external sources, or write code.

items.prompt: What is the problem with this class?
items.answer: Rather than choosing a function by name, choose it by the nature of the job. Considering how long the task is and how much evidence is needed makes the choice easier.

screens.outro: First, let me think of the task I want to entrust.

screens.title: Think back: Something that took a long time with Excel
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: If AI could do the organizing that used to take a long time in Excel, what task would you want to do?
items.answer: Common examples include merging multiple sheets, unifying column names, calculating monthly totals, and finding unusual values. The more repetitive a task is and the more clear the rules are, the better it is to entrust.

items.prompt: What are the inputs to that task and what should the output look like?
items.answer: If the input is a file I own, the function that handles the file is correct. If the input is multiple external sites, it is the function that collects the sources. Whether the results are tables, charts, or reports with citations is also a clue to your choice.

items.prompt: What do you need to trust and use the results?
items.answer: If it is a calculation result, it must show what method was used, and if it is a research result, what the source is. This lesson covers how to verify evidence in both cases.

screens.outro: Now let's look at data analysis and Codex.

screens.title: Data analysis and Codex
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the distinction between Codex and Work, which input fits well with the work of data analysis.

visual.alt: Mockup screen showing the uploaded table and generated charts in the Data Analysis dialog.
labels: Summarize monthly sales and find outliers
View the code used for analysis

tabs.label: data analysis
tabs.body: ChatGPT looks at uploaded files, answers questions about your data, and creates tables or charts when a structured view would be helpful. For the best results, be specific about what you want to know, what columns or calculations to use, what criteria to group by, and what type of chart to use. Files can be spreadsheets such as .xls, .xlsx, and .csv, as well as files such as PDF, .json, .xml, .yaml, .txt, and .md. The range of support may vary depending on model, plan, and settings.

tabs.label: good input
tabs.body: The shape of the input determines the result. Put descriptive column names in the first row, contain one record per row, and write the column names in simple words. Conversely, avoid placing multiple unrelated tables on one sheet, separating data with empty rows and columns, or containing values ​​to be analyzed within an image. These three are the main reasons why ChatGPT misreads the structure.

tabs.label: What you can do
tabs.body: Data analysis allows you to summarize rows and columns, trends, and outliers, create tables for row review, draw charts, use Python to perform calculations and transformations, perform statistical analysis, and explain assumptions, results, and next steps. Some tasks require ChatGPT to write and run Python code, reviewing the generated code, output, and assumptions before writing the results. If the method is important, ask ChatGPT to show you the method or change it.

tabs.label: chart
tabs.body: Charts are primarily images, and some can also be viewed as interactive charts. Select Switch to interactive chart if an interactive chart is available, or Switch to static chart to return to the image. Interactive charts support bar, line, circle, and scatterplots; other types can be returned as images.

tabs.label: Codex
tabs.body: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent that helps you write, review, and deploy code. Log in with your ChatGPT account and use it in the desktop app, CLI, IDE extension, and web, and is included in ChatGPT plans including Free and Go. Codex Cloud is only available on select eligible plans and is not included in Free and Go. Usage limits vary by plan.

tabs.label: Chat·Work·Codex
tabs.body: ChatGPT includes Chat and Work. Chat is for quick, interactive help and everyday questions, while Work is your agent for long, multi-step tasks and finished deliverables. Codex remains dedicated to software development and technical work. Therefore, for general long tasks that do not involve writing code, think of Work, not Codex.

screens.outro: Next, we will look at the flow of in-depth research that synthesizes external sources.

screens.title: Flow of in-depth research and relationship with plan
screens.lead: The following steps show the sequence in which in-depth research occurs. Select the next arrow to follow step by step.

visual.alt: A horizontal flowchart of the five stages of in-depth research.

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: In-depth research is the ability to make inferences, investigate, and synthesize information to create a written report. Handle complex online tasks across uploaded files, the public web or specific sites, and ChatGPT apps you are permitted to use. It is a tool for multi-step research rather than one short question.

steps.title: 1) Describe the desired result
steps.body: First, describe the results you need. The more specifically you write down the target, item, and result type, such as 'a comparison table of the prices and characteristics of five competing services with sources,' the more accurate the direction of the research will be.

steps.title: 2) Specify a site or file
steps.body: If necessary, select a reference website or uploaded file. By default, you can use the public web, uploaded files, and connected apps. Connected apps can be used automatically when permissions and workspace settings allow, and app linking does not replace the provider's permissions.

steps.title: 3) Receiving and revising the research plan
steps.body: ChatGPT suggests a research plan before you begin your research. People can review and fix this plan. If you figure out which items to research and correct any missing perspectives at this stage, you won't waste a lot of work.

steps.title: 4) Change direction while watching progress
steps.body: You can monitor the investigation as it progresses and step in at any time to change focus or adjust which sources you can access. It is not a tool that you have to wait until the end once you start it.

steps.title: 5) Receive a report with citations
steps.body: The results are returned as a structured report with citations and links to sources. The goal is to make the information verifiable, so we'll open the link to the source and compare the important figures directly.

steps.title: What question does it answer, and what is its relationship to the plan?
steps.body: In-depth research is perfect for deep questions that require analysis by combining multiple sources, especially when you want to have control over which sources you use. A quick check-in or short conversation may be faster than a regular conversation. Start by typing /Deepresearch or from the Tools menu or sidebar. Usage depends on your plan and you can check the remaining count with a counter on the screen. The scope and limits of data analysis and Codex usage vary depending on the plan and settings.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the nature of the three functions, let’s apply them to one task.

screens.title: Narrative Case Study: What to Write in a Market Research Report
screens.lead: The instructor will walk you through the process of choosing the right features for your market research report work. Select the next arrow to follow the basis for your decision.

steps.title: read request
steps.body: The request is 'a report summarizing the prices and features of five competing services with sources.' Candidates are General Conversation, Data Analysis, Codex, and In-Depth Research. The request is judged not by name but by two characteristics: the length of the work and the basis for the request.

steps.title: Step 1: View the length of the task
steps.body: Researching the five requires reading, itemizing, and synthesizing multiple sources. These are not short questions that check one or two facts. This includes the manual work of opening dozens of sites and comparing them. This multi-step task is the scope of in-depth research.

steps.title: Step 2: View supporting claims
steps.body: Reports require sources. This is because you need to be able to check where the numbers come from before you can use them as a report. In-depth research fits this need because it returns a structured report with citations or source links.

steps.title: Step 3: Eliminate other candidates
steps.body: General conversation is good for quickly confirming one or two facts, but is narrow in scope for an investigation that synthesizes five points. Data analysis is a function that deals with files I own, so it is not suitable for collecting external sources. Codex is an agent that handles code work and is not intended for market research.

steps.title: Step 4: Confirm your plan and narrow it down
steps.body: When you begin in-depth research, a research plan is first proposed. Check that all five locations are included and that prices and features are itemized, and revise the plan if necessary. Narrowing down your search by specifying reliable official sites can increase the reliability of your results. If you have a file, you can upload data such as an internal price list to compare the results of the investigation, or refer to the documentation of the permitted app.

steps.title: Step 5: Make adjustments along the way
steps.body: If a service is missing or the direction is off during the investigation, change focus midway through. You don't have to wait until the end to follow your initial plan. The longer the investigation, the greater the value of intermediate checks, and once the direction is off, the more time is wasted, so adjusting the sources you can access can also be done at this stage. For example, if a site with a lot of advertising content is mixed in, we request that the source be excluded and the site narrowed down to the official site.

steps.title: Step 6: Verify results
steps.body: The prices and figures in the received report can be directly compared by opening the source link. If the publication date of the source is old or it is not an official site, mark the figure separately and check again. Even if the report has citations, verification is a human responsibility. If necessary, you can continue using the function by uploading the downloaded table to data analysis and organizing it into totals or charts.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: In-depth research made sense in this case because the work was long, required synthesis of multiple sources, and the evidence was important. Conversely, if you only want to confirm one fact, regular conversation is faster. It is not the name that determines the function, but the length of the work and its rationale requirements. Just ask the same question. Is this task short or long, does it need a basis, is the input from my file or an external source?

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the criteria for feature selection, let's summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Summary: length and basis determine function
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Please read while thinking about whether your research work is a short confirmation or a long synthesis.

paragraphs: Data analysis is a function that turns the tables you upload into summaries, calculations, and charts. The results are good when the first row contains descriptive column names and the structure contains one record per row. If you analyzed in Python, review the code and assumptions and write the results.

Codex is a coding agent that helps you write, review, and deploy code and is used in software development and technical tasks. ChatGPT's Work handles long, multi-step general tasks and results that don't involve writing code.

In-depth research involves creating a research plan, synthesizing multiple sources, and producing a report with citations. The unique feature is that you can revise your plan and change direction mid-flight, and a regular conversation can be faster for quick confirmations.

The range and usage limits for all three features vary depending on your plan and settings. Which function is appropriate is determined by the length of the task and the needs of the rationale, not by the name.

In practice, functions are often used interchangeably. This involves collecting data with provenance through in-depth research, organizing the results in tables, and then compiling them through data analysis. All you have to do is follow the flow of human verification of the results of each step. Even in this case, there is no confusion if you keep in mind that the inputs for the file upload function and the external inspection function are different, and Codex is in charge of writing the code.

Lastly, keep in mind the cost and limit perspectives as well. In-depth research has a usage amount for each plan and the remaining count is displayed as a counter on the screen, so if you use it for a short check, you will be wasting the count. Codex also has a usage limit for each plan, so choosing the function that suits the depth you need is the easiest way to save on the limit. It is also helpful to have the habit of checking the screen to see if your limit is remaining.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: Whichever function you use, the method for checking the basis for the results is different. Data analysis identifies codes and assumptions, and in-depth research identifies source links.

glossary.def: OpenAI's coding agent that helps you write, review, and deploy code. Log in with your ChatGPT account to write.
This function examines uploaded files, answers questions, and converts them into tables, charts, and calculations.
This is the function to create a research plan, synthesize multiple sources, and create a report with citations or source links.
A list of research steps suggested by In-Depth Research before beginning the investigation, which can be reviewed and modified by humans.
This agent is responsible for long, multi-step tasks and completed results within ChatGPT.

misconceptions.myth: Data analysis is good at reading any table.
misconceptions.fact: For good results, the column names and row structure must be clear. Tables that are mixed together unrelated, have many blank rows and columns, or contain images of values ​​are difficult to read.

misconceptions.myth: In-depth research is always better than general search.
misconceptions.fact: In-depth research is for questions that require deep, multiple sources. A quick check-in or short conversation may be faster than a regular conversation.

misconceptions.myth: Codex is a separate service that cannot be used unless you know coding.
misconceptions.fact: Codex is a coding agent that you use by logging in with your ChatGPT account. However, since it is used for code work, Work takes over the long tasks of general tasks without code.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Data analysis turns your tables into summaries, calculations, and charts.
Codex is a coding agent that works on your code.
In-depth research is ideal for investigations that require lengthy synthesis and links to sources.
The length of the work and the needs for the basis determine the function, and the scope of use is determined by the plan and settings.

checks.q: What is the most appropriate table to upload to the data analysis function?
options: File with multiple unrelated tables scattered on one sheet
A table with descriptive column names in the first row and one record per row.
Table divided into sections by empty rows and empty columns
checks.explain: Descriptive column names in the first row and a row-by-record structure are good inputs. The rest are forms to be avoided.

wrong.0: If there are multiple unrelated tables, the results will be blurred.
wrong.1: Values in images are difficult to read and should be avoided.
wrong.3: Empty rows and columns obscure the structure and should be avoided.

checks.intro: The shape of the table used for data analysis determines the quality of the results. Choose the right ticket.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. A table with descriptive column names in the first row and one record per row is a good input.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The remaining views have scattered structures, images of values, or sections divided by blank cells. Look again at one record per row.

checks.q: Get the flow of writing in-depth research in the right order
items: Monitor progress and change direction if necessary
Receive reports with citations and links to sources
checks.explain: After explaining the results and setting the scope, confirming the plan, adjusting the direction along the way, and receiving a report with sources attached.
checks.intro: Arrange the steps of in-depth research in order.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. You've got the flow of a report outlining goals, specifying scope, revising the plan, making adjustments along the way, and attaching sources.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. The plan is checked and revised before the investigation begins, and the report is the final result.

checks.q: You need to organize the prices and features of five competing services along with their sources. What is the best choice?
options: Quickly confirm one or two facts in a general conversation
Entrust the writing of the report to Codex
Use data analysis to turn posted tables into charts
Comprehend through in-depth research and check the numbers with source links.
checks.explain: In-depth research is appropriate because it requires reading, synthesizing, and citing multiple sources. Check the figures in the received report by clicking the source link.

wrong.0: General conversation is better suited for short fact-checking.
wrong.1: Codex is a coding agent and is not intended for market research.
wrong.2: Data analysis is a function that deals with uploaded files and is not intended to synthesize external sources.

checks.intro: It is a research task that requires synthesizing multiple sources. Choose the right features.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. In-depth research is appropriate for tasks that require reading, synthesizing, and citing multiple sources.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The functions Dialog for quick fact-checking, Codex for working with code, and analyzing tables have different purposes from this task. Start by determining whether synthesis and citation are necessary.
